A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods and substantial overlap in experiments. The complete main text, figures, tables, equation, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, training ablations, COCO retrieval-error annotations, and an appendix audit of ARO labels.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds the authors' SugarCrepe evaluation in Table 2.

M1.justification: The grounded recaptioning procedure, pretrained text encoders, last-four-layer fine-tuning, contrastive objective, sentence sampling, and hard-negative training remain unchanged. SugarCrepe evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds SugarCrepe, extending compositionality evaluation to more plausible negative captions across object, attribute, and relation replacement, swapping, and addition. This is a focused extension within the existing image–text task; previous training and evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds Vera to the ARO comparison and reports SugarCrepe comparisons including DC-XL, LAION, CapPa, GPT-4V, and humans. Gemini-text's ARO result already appeared in v1's prose. Table 2's row labeled CLIP cites the ALIGN reference, leaving that row's attribution unclear.

E3.justification: The added SugarCrepe comparison documents different input conditions: Vera receives text only, while GPT-4V sees both candidate captions simultaneously. Existing training budgets, retrieval settings, ImageNet evaluation, and human-audit procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The language-shortcut analysis is extended through Vera's above-chance ARO scores and approximately chance-level SugarCrepe scores. The original Gemini text-only probe, method ablations, COCO error analysis, and appendix left/right-label audit remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The ImageNet two-proportion z-test and Appendix C's caption-distribution estimation remain unchanged. v2 introduces no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: New SugarCrepe results report 97/94/88% for replacement, 89/94% for swapping, and 95/93% for addition. Vera's ARO results of 62% relations and 83% attributes are also added. Matched retrieval, ImageNet, ablation, and appendix results retain their previous values.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. Appendix C retains the same sequence log-likelihood equation.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the broad claim of surpassing all bespoke architectures with a benchmark-specific state-of-the-art claim naming ARO and SugarCrepe. The central contributions concerning richer captions, stronger semantic guidance, and COCO's limitations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains how SugarCrepe's plausible negatives mitigate the language-only shortcut already acknowledged for ARO. It also adds a GPT-4V superiority statement that slightly overstates Table 2: the reported scores show five wins, one tie, and one loss.

D1.justification: Table 2 identifies the LAION comparator as xlm-roberta-large-ViT-H-14 and specifies comparator input access. Existing implementation details, accelerator counts, training schedules, recaptioning prompts, and appendix scoring instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SugarCrepe, Vera, DataComp, LAION-5B, and the GPT-4 technical report, and removes the Brendel–Bethge bag-of-local-features citation. Section 3.1 adds positioning against captioning-based training; the broader related-work narrative remains stable.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the abstract, expanded Section 3.1, and small discussion and cross-reference corrections. Google DeepMind affiliation text is added. The section sequence and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with red and blue modality markers and an updated caption. Table 1 gains Gemini-text and Vera rows, and SugarCrepe receives a new Table 2. Existing figures and tables are otherwise retained, with float relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: SugarCrepe provides useful additional validation beyond ARO's acknowledged language-only shortcuts: the proposed model performs strongly while Vera remains near chance. This limited evidential gain outweighs the new reporting flaws, including the CLIP/ALIGN citation mismatch and overstated GPT-4V win count. The method and earlier results remain unchanged.
